articleTitle: Simulation And Experimental Research Of 1d Metallodielectric Photonic Crystals In The Millimetre Waveband
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The research presented in this report reveals some of the prospectives of using nanometer metallic layers in photonic crystals. The simulation and experimental measurements have been performed in the millimeter and sub-millimeter wavelength ranges for one-dimensional structures comprised of quartz, teflon and bismuth. It is shown that thin metallic films can be used to smoothen the reflectivity spectrum and narrow the main reflectivity.

articleTitle: Modeling of 1-D photonic bandgap microstrip structures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: In this paper, it is presented a two-sided one-dimensional photonic bandgap microstrip structure. The structure is obtained by etching a one periodic pattern of circles in the ground plane of a microstrip line and variation of the characteristic impedance as a function of the length of the microstrip line. The calculated scattering parameters of the proposed filter are presented.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of the quantum efficiency of InGaAs/GaAs resonant cavity enhanced photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: We present a theoretical analysis on the quantum efficiency of a resonant cavity InGaAs/GaAs p-i-n photodetector (PD) for the ultrashort optical connections. The numerical method of calculation of quantum efficiency combining a transfer matrix method and a energy conservation law is offered. Using anomalous dispersion (AD) mirror as the top mirror flat-topped QE spectrum has been obtained. Conditions for ideal flat-topped the spectral response have been received. We present a design with a maximum QE of 93.5% and 3 nm bandwidth at 0.02 dB below the peak.

articleTitle: Modeling, Analysis and Optimization of Chirped Mirrors
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The model for interaction of an ultrashort optical pulse with chirped mirror is developed through exact analysis of the pulse waveform. This allows to optimize chirped mirror design in terms of pulse parameters (duration, time-bandwidth product, energy dissipation, FWHM, RMS). Cases of single mirror, double mirror, normal and oblique incidence, s-and p-polarizations are considered. The problem of mirror optimization is examined. Titanium dioxide and silicon nitride structures oriented to lambda= 800 nm are compared.

articleTitle: Nanolithography ߝ nanoimprinting
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: In the article are represented the analysis of existent methods of nanolithography on the example of nanoimprinting, features of technological processes with the use of nanoimprinting, advantages and lacks of different methods and direction of their application are appraised.

articleTitle: Experience of work of Research& Technical Centre "Thermocontrol" in the Area of thermal non-destructive Test and Thernography
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Thermal non-destructive testing (TNDT) is one of the well-known and dynamically developing in the world methods of controlling the quality of materials and goods. TNDT is based on the registration of temperature fields, which are generated on the surface of tested objects in result of their forced heating (this direction is called the active thermal test) or in result of its functioning (this direction is called thermography). Research & technical centre "Thermocontrol" deals with thermal non-destructive test and thermography more than 30 years. The Centre is certified by National Cosmic Agency of Ukraine (NCAU) No. 000084 for the right to carrying out works in the area of space technology. Two specialists of the 3rd TNDT level are certified by ISO version.

articleTitle: A new approach to polarization hologram registration
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: A new approach to formation and registration of polarization hologram on periodic layer structures is presented. A structure with alternate photosensitive layers, containing bacteriorodopsin, and transparent isotropic layers is considered. Such structure corresponds to an uniaxial quasicrystal with form birefringence. In the quasicrystal registration of polarization hologram is ensured by ordinary and extraordinary waves, having orthogonal polarizations.

articleTitle: Macroporous Silicon Infiltrated with Liquid Crystals: Director-Field Configuration and Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: We present the simulated distribution of the local director of nematic liquid crystal (NLC) which is confined inside cylindrical macropores of the porous silicon. The Frank free energy approach is used to describe the NLC in porous medium. The influence of molecular anchoring strength and external electric field applied is investigated. Bruggeman approximation is used while calculating effective refractive index of each layer in porous silicon multilayer structure. Reflectivity spectrum of the latter is simulated using transfer matrix approach. Electrical tuning range of microcavity designed for resonance at 1330 nm vary from 8.5 nm up to 16 nm for weak and strong surface anchoring conditions respectively.

articleTitle: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy for quantitative measurement of metals alloys components
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The major advantage of LIBS compared to other analytical techniques is that no time-consuming sample preparation is necessary. LIBS use the plasma generated by a high-energy laser beam to prepare and excite the sample in one step. It has the ability to perform multielement real-time analysis. An experimental method have been developed and practical results have been obtained for silver, gold and copper alloys.

articleTitle: Automatization Of The Control Technological Processes Of Optical Fiber Components Parameters
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Object of researches are the control processes of optical fiber components parameters. The purpose of researches is development of the theory and methods bases which allow solving of the scientific -applied problem of the control processes automation of constructive -technological parameters in manufacture, installation and exploitation of passive optical fiber components, to create of theoretical and practical base for modules designing of the automated technological complexes. The research methods are the optical television methods of images and optical fields recognition, the methods of the return problems decision, the Fourier-analysis, the theory of analytical signals and Hilbert's transformation, the methods of an optimum filtration, the regressive analysis and imitating modeling. The results practical importance is developing of the automated technologies, automated modules and managing programs of the control of optical fiber components constructive -technological parameters. The novelty of research results is advancement of the automated control theory of a refraction index profile of light guide structures with use of a near field technique; is development of the interference control theory of surfaces form factors of switching optical fiber components; is the advancement of the positioning automated control theory of an optical fiber in cylindrical armature; is provided the further development of the automated control theory of optical fibers positioning parameters during welding.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of optical processes in nonlinear photonic crystals devices
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: In the work, there have been developed the theoretical method based on the FDTD method for the investigation of optical characteristics in nonlinear photonic crystals. Moreover, in the work it have been developed optical power limiters on the basis of 1D and 2D nonlinear photonic crystals and their characteristics studied.

articleTitle: Education and simulations with LaserCADIII
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The LaserCADIII is software that has been developed for high speed simulation of base characteristics of bulk and quantum-well semiconductor lasers. The algorithm of the software is based on modern theory of semiconductor laser including rate equation, band structure theory, gain theory and semiconductor alloy engineering. LaserCADIII can be applied both for scientific simulation and education aims.

articleTitle: Efficient gain computation for semiconductor quantum-wells
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: We propose efficient method for gain computation in semiconductor low-dimension structures. The method is based on combination of finite-difference method and variational technique. Computations are accompanied by interpolation procedure to increase computation speed.

articleTitle: Effects of electric fields on nematic liquid crystals with dispersed carbon nanotubes: conductivity and capacitance measurements
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Electrophysical properties of dispersions of carbon nanotubes in cyanobiphenyl-based nematic liquid crystals were studied under d.c. voltage (50 micron thick layers). The observed behavior was strongly sensitive to NT concentration. The obtained results are interpreted in terms of molecular models, and possible applications in electronic devices are discussed.

articleTitle: Highly efficient resonant-cavity light-emitting diodes for compact color projectors
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: An overview of red-green-blue highly efficient resonant-cavity light-emitting diodes is presented. First, the main parameters of dipole emission in planar cavities are reviewed. From these, we derive design rules to improve the device external efficiency. We point out some guidelines for comparison of light-emitting diodes, and use these to review the different device structures in different material systems and at different wavelengths.

articleTitle: Laser dyes. Quest and development in IRE NASU
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Numerous studies of novel active media for dye lasers fulfilled in IRE NASU are generalized in present work. Peculiarities of spectral, fluorescence, and lasing characteristics of some laser dye classes for visible region of the spectrum have been analysed. A special attention is focused upon effects of structure of dye molecule and its solvent environment on these characteristics.

articleTitle: New trends in analytical applications of aqueous electrogenerated chemiluminescence
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: We give brief overview of new approaches and technologies for fabrication of electrochemiluminescent (ECL) devices for different application. New method of ECL generation in aqueous mediums as well as results of recent experiments and their potential applications, including highly sensitive optical analysis of liquid mediums, will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Electronic and optical properties on non-polar InGaN/GaN quantum-well structures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Electronic and optical properties of non-polar (112 macr0) a-(phi=0), (101macr0) m-plane (phi=pi/6), and (1122 macr)-oriented wurtzite (WZ) InGaN/GaN quantum well (QW) structures are investigated using the multiband effective-mass theory. These results are compared with those of (0001)-oriented WZ InGaN/GaN QW structures. The internal field becomes zero for (1122 macr) crystal orientation near the crystal angle of thetas=56deg, in addition to a-and m-plane with thetas=90deg irrespective of the In composition in the well. This is because the sum of the piezoelectric and spontaneous polarizations in the barrier is equal to that in the well. The optical gain of QW structures with non-polar crystal orientation is significantly larger than that of the (0001)-oriented QW. This is caused mainly by the increase of the optical matrix element due to the disappearance of the internal field. Also, the (1122 macr)-oriented QW is found to have the optical gain comparable to the a-or m-plane QW. In addition, their optical matrix element show strong in-plane anisotropy. The bandgap transition wavelength of the QW structure with the m-plane is found to be longer than that of the QW structures with the a-plane.

articleTitle: Simulation of Active Regions of Semiconductor Lasers and Optical Amplifiers based on Quantum Wells
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Simulation of band structure, potential profile and carrier transport in QWs are highlighted. Anisotropy of the valence band on the density of states and gain spectra of QWs is addressed. It has been shown that axial approximation leads to underestimated gain. Errors can amount to 18.8%. Results of selfconsistent computation of energy band diagram for compositionally asymmetric multiple quantum-well structure are presented. Flat-band approximation of quantum-well potential profile is examined. Quantum capture and tunneling in SQWs and MQWs are considered. It is shown that tunneling do play significant role in high-speed properties of (A)MQW SOA and prediction of SOA gain spectrum. Is is shown that quantum capture area is a function of temperature and injection level, and consequently is governed by composition and structure of a QW-device and its operating point.

articleTitle: Application of the digital holographic interference microscope for thin films investigation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: We used the digital holographic interference microscope (DHIM) for thin films investigation. Three-dimensional (3-D) image of A1N thin film deposited on an acryl substrate by vacuum-arc method .and the results of the film thickness measurement are presented. It has been shown that the DHIM can be successfully used for film surface quality control, thickness and film damages parameters measurement.

articleTitle: To the question of quantum cryptography transmission system with polarized coding development
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: There is analysed the existing methods of stability increase for key transmission of quantum cryptographic optical communication system with polarized coding. Also there is estimated the mode dispersion delay for the modern optical fibers, used in communication system range 150-200 km, in comparison to coherency interval of semiconductor lasers, based on GaAs. The recommendations of optic using of optical fibers and lasers for real quantum cryptography systems are given.

articleTitle: Passive fiber-optical components based on the potonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Transmission spectrums and losses of the different kinds of the planar photonic crystal (PhC) waveguides and tapers are calculated and compared. Some of these components have been fabricated and measured. The most efficient type of the taper is one based on the photonic band-gap (PBG) effect and waveguide with widened core region.

articleTitle: Optical logic gate `AND', controllable photon crystal
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: An amorphous dielectric film with reflecting cross edges can be considered as the Fabry-Perot resonator with flat mirrors. The presence or absence of the polariton field maxima or zeros on output mirror we regard as the signals in the optical logic gate based on dielectric film. The photon crystal is formed in the dielectric film if the pump electromagnetic wave generates the superlattice and the signal electromagnetic wave is scattering at the lattice. The shape of the superlattice can change in dependence on the value of electrostatic field, and it leads to the boundaries changing of allowed and forbidden zones of the wave signal spectrum in the photon crystals.

articleTitle: Impact of position-dependent effective mass on injector transmissivity in the quantum-cascade laser
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Design of the electron injector influences the threshold current, dynamic characteristics and efficiency of quantum cascade lasers. We aim to determine the impact of the position-dependent effective mass on transmissivity of the injector in quantum-cascade laser.

articleTitle: Effective-mass superlattice as a ballistic transport element
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The new structure for management of carriers' ballistic transport have been proposed. This structure is based on effective-mass superlattice. The paper contains results which represent transmission coefficient spectra corresponding to center and non-center ballistic transport in considered structure.

articleTitle: Novel Optoelectronic Elements based on Asymmetric Multiple-Quantum-Well Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Main attention is devoted to results in the study of dynamic and spectral characteristics of the asymmetric multiple-quantum-well heterostructure (AMQWH) lasers with active regions of different widths and compositions. Recent results in development of superluminescence diodes, polarization insensitive optical amplifiers, broadband tunable laser diodes, quantum cascade lasers, and other optoelectronic elements, including their various applications are also shortly indicated.

articleTitle: Recent Advances of VCSEL technology at GIST
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The insatiable demand for higher bandwidth in optical communication systems and newly emerging various non communication applications of VCSELs are spurring the development of VCSELs with higher performances and functions. In this presentation, we will describe recent advances of VCSEL technology at GIST in terms of operation speed, single transverse mode operation, polarization stabilization, and output beam shaping. The developed VCSELs have unique features that have been gradually implemented for high performance systems, such as optical interconnects, miniature atomic clocks, gas sensors, and biosensors.

articleTitle: Possibility of temperature regime expansion in near-an mid MQ lasers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: It is observed the existing methods of temperature regime expansion in MQW lasers of near-and mid-IR semiconductor heterostructures. Also it is shown new possibilities to extend working temperatures of the considered devices.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Simulation of Semiconductor Lasers and Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers using ATLAS
publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: The ridge-waveguide semiconductor laser and amplifier is simulated. Comparison of simulation results of static characteristics to experiment has shown good agreement. Simple physical picture of SOA recovery is developed and it shows that any alternation of the carrier lifetimes in the active region of SOA can be used for speed-up of device response. Various combinations of active region doping have been considered as a way of recovery acceleration. Simulation of SOA response shows that using homogeneous doping of active layer, speed-up of the SOA response can be achieved. Doping of a thin part of the active layer results in smaller speed-up, as compared to the case of the whole active layer doping. Relative position of doped layer within the active layer plays no role in response acceleration.

publicationTitle: 2007 International Workshop on Optoelectronic Physics and Technology
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members and society officers.

abstract: Prospective authors are requested to submit new, unpublished manuscripts for inclusion in the upcoming event described in this call for papers.
